items.title: John Altman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 14, 2023
items.q: And all he wanted to talk about was the Lionel Hampton band and Clifford Brown and Jimmy Cleveland

ctx.x: I’m trying to imagine what you and Quincy Jones would talk about. I had made an assumption early on in this project that musicians when they get together always talk about music. And then I overheard a conversation once with Frank Wess and Joe Williams and a number of other fellas like that and they weren’t talking about music at all.

Yeah. Well funny enough the great thing about talking with Quincy was I happened to mention Lucky Thompson straight off the bat which of course set him off. And all he wanted to talk about was the Lionel Hampton band and Clifford Brown and Jimmy Cleveland and it was, I’m sure everybody else at the table, I mean it was a big event. And we talked the whole evening. And I don’t think we got any later than 1956. And it was wonderful you know because I suppose nobody ever spoke to him about that anymore you know it…

Well I want to go back with you because I read that you came from a musical family and your uncles were in the business. Were you fascinated early on by — how much did you witness of what they did and was it something that seemed like oh yes, I want to do that.
